s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
abnormal laboratory findings including leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia
key_facts: 10-day history of fever
tender lesions on the neck and trunk
past medical history of IgG-κ multiple myeloma
recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers
white blood cell count: 2.3 × 10^3/μL
hemoglobin: 12.1 g/dL
platelet count: 29 × 10^3/μL
C-reactive protein: 3.31 mg/dL
blood culture: negative
skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: fever, tender skin lesions, and recent chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
shortlist.why_kept: febrile illness, skin lesions, and recent chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers

shortlist.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: history of multiple myeloma and skin lesions

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, tender lesions on the neck and trunk, and laboratory findings such as a low white blood cell count and elevated C-reactive protein, along with the skin biopsy showing an inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells and positive immunohistochemistry for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, are consistent with Sweet syndrome, especially in the context of a recent chemotherapy cycle for multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
rejected.why: While it can occur in the setting of chemotherapy, the clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not specifically align with neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis, which typically involves the eccrine glands.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: Erythema multiforme typically presents with target lesions and is often associated with infections or medications, but the biopsy findings and clinical context in this case are more suggestive of Sweet syndrome.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: The biopsy did not show obvious leukocytoclastic vasculitis, and the clinical presentation and other findings are not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The immunohistochemistry results, particularly the negativity for CD138, do not support a diagnosis of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma, and the clinical presentation is not consistent with this rare and aggressive lymphoma.
